questions.prompt: What is the capital city of East Timor?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the East Timor article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city, Dili, is home to one hundred and fifty thousand people.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with East Timor?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture East Timor on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the East Timor article.

questions.proof: Australia, a large nearby country, sent troops in to make peace.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of East Timor?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the East Timor article.

questions.proof: It is a member of the United Nations, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and the Community of Portuguese Language Countries.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “At the time, the United States government said it did not know _____ was going to invade East Timor.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “know”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the East Timor article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1975, the Portuguese army left, and East Timor was invaded (taken over) by the Indonesian army in 1975.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “For a long time, _____ controlled the East Timor and called it the Colony of Portuguese Timor.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “controlled”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the East Timor article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: For a long time, Portugal controlled the East Timor and called it the Colony of Portuguese Timor.
